title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms (v1)
authors: Jonathan Luk, Sung-Jin Oh, Shiwu Yang
section_locator: Title page through Section 1.1: abstract; metric ansatz g=-Omega^2 du.dv + r^2 dsigma; Hawking mass definition (1.2); system (SSESF) (all four equations); normalization (dr|_{C_u0}=1/2, r(u0,u0)=m(u0,u0)=0); Theorem 1.1 with (1.7)-(1.9); Remarks 1.2-1.3
assumptions_read: Characteristic data Phi on C_{u0} with (1.7); conclusion (1.8): dr/dv>1/3, -2/3<dr/du<-1/6, 2m/r<1/2; (1.9): |phi|, |d_v(rphi)|, |d_u(rphi)| and pure second derivatives |d_v^2(rphi)|+|d_v^2 r|+|d_u^2(rphi)|+|d_u^2 r| bounded by C*eps uniformly in u0
conclusion_for_this_lane: Verbatim confirmation that the coordinator's displayed equations match LOY: mass equations are (d_a r)(d_a m)=(1/2)(1-2m/r)r^2(d_a phi)^2, i.e. m_v=(1-mu)r^2 phi_v^2/(2 lambda); r_uv=2m nulambda/((1-mu)r^2); and (r phi)_uv=r_uv phi is LOY's own second SSESF equation. Nondegeneracy constants match (lambda>1/3 gives a=2lambda>2/3).
proof_status: Not assessed; proofs are in Sections 2-6 which were not fetched. This record pins equations/statements only.
dependencies: Christodoulou [2,4] small-data and BV results as cited by LOY

Does the global two-sided solution class (Theorem 1.7) carry the global a>=2/3 bound used for clock unboundedness?
